title: Eggs, Grade A, Large, egg yolk

content.title: About
content.content: Grade A large eggs are top‑quality eggs from healthy hens. The yolk is bright orange, nutrient‑dense, and has a delicate flavor. These eggs are ideal for cooking, baking, and even raw consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A typical large Grade A egg weighs about 63–73 g.
The yolk contains almost all of the egg’s nutrients – vitamins, minerals, and fats.
Hens that lay Grade A eggs are often fed specially formulated feeds enriched with omega‑3 and lutein.
Eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 weeks if they are not washed before storage.
Egg grading standards vary by country, but Grade A always denotes the highest quality.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: One large egg provides about 6 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: The yolk is one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, supporting bone health and immunity.

items.title: Contains choline
items.content: Choline is important for brain function and liver health; a single egg supplies over 30 % of the daily requirement.

items.title: Lutein and zeaxanthin
items.content: These carotenoids protect eyesight and reduce the risk of age‑related eye diseases.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: An egg contains roughly 70 kcal, making it a convenient option for weight management.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Egg white proteins can trigger severe allergic reactions, especially in children.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Raw or undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella; it is recommended to cook eggs thoroughly.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains about 186 mg of cholesterol; individuals with high cholesterol should moderate intake.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: When buying, check for intact shells and avoid cracked eggs to prevent contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eggs can be boiled, fried, poached, used in sauces, mayonnaise, desserts, omelets, and salads. The yolk is often separated for custards, sauces, and baking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store eggs in their original carton in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Do not wash them before storage to preserve the natural protective coating. Use within 4‑5 weeks.
